newsitem.title: FINLAND: Raisio says J&J deal to boost '97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Raisio says J&J deal to boost '97 earnings.

text.p: Finnish food group Raision Tehtaat said on Friday its cooperation with U.S. group Johnson & Johnson would help its earnings this year, and that it would get upfront payment upon government approval of the deal.

"The agreement provides Raisio Group with an upfront payment upon government approval of the deal, additional payments in subsequent years tied to performance, royalties on sales of Benecol products and manufacturing profits for stanol ester," it said.
Raisio announced on July 15 an agreement which gives Johnson & Johnson company McNeil Consumer Products exclusive rights to the patents and trademark of the Benecol cholesterol-reducing agent.
"The agreeement will benefit Raisio group profits already this year," it said.
Raisio has said earlier it expects its full-1997 financial performance to improve on last year and that it targets net sales of five billion markka, up from last year's 3.93 billion.
In 1996, Raisio posted a 166.4 million markka profit before extraordinary items, and in January-April this year, its profit before extras rose to 69.4 million markka from 51.5 million a year earlier.
